Meeting header:
Date: 2025-11-07
Time: 14:00 PT
Duration: ~38 minutes
Location: Zoom (recording)
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Sofia Patel (Redwood SE), Maya Alvarez (Sunnyside Head of Product), Dr. Kevin Li (Sunnyside CTO), Jordan Brooks (Sunnyside Marketing)

Summary: Short-form podcast-style interview recorded for marketing/case study. Focus on how Sunnyside uses Redwood for conversational triage and clinician support, measurable latency/cost wins, and security posture for healthcare data. Audio will be edited for podcast; transcript contains some auto-transcription errors.

Topics: use case overview, migration story, performance metrics, security & compliance, marketing outcomes, next steps for publish/approval.

0:00 - Alex Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, this is Alex from Redwood, umm we're recording this as a friendly podcast-style interview. Quick audio check?
0:12 - Maya Alvarez: Audio's good here, hey Alex, excited to chat.
0:20 - Jordan Brooks: Good morning / afternoon, all good.
0:34 - Alex Chen: Quick intro — Sofia is our solutions engineer who worked on the initial POC, I'll ask her to drop a couple numbers later. Sofia, want to say hi?
0:44 - Sofia Patel: Hey Maya, Kevin, Jordan, great to be here. Kevin you did the heavy lifting with the infra so thanks for that.
0:52 - Dr. Kevin Li: Thanks, yeah, appreciate the help.
1:10 - Alex Chen: Cool, we're gonna keep this conversational — if anything off the record just tell us. Start by, Maya, can you give a two-sentence about Sunnyside and the problem you were solving?
1:24 - Maya Alvarez: Sure, Sunnyside is a virtual behavioral health platform, we connect patients to clinicians and provide guided CBT exercises. We were getting overwhelmed on intake flows, long wait times, repetitive triage questions that clinicians had to sift through. We wanted to automate the initial triage but keep safety and clinician oversight.
1:46 - Alex Chen: Nice, and timeline — when did you start engaging with Redwood?
1:52 - Maya Alvarez: We started a small POC in March, sort of exploratory, then ramped in May to production.
2:03 - Jordan Brooks: From a marketing lens, we also wanted to talk about this for a case study because adoption metrics were good.
2:15 - Alex Chen: Sofia, could you describe the POC briefly and the infra choices?
2:22 - Sofia Patel: Sure — we ran a dedicated POC on Redwood Dedicated capacity, used a small reserved pool of A100-ish GPUs, emulated peak windows. We tested streaming responses for the triage chat, used prefix caching for repeated prompts, and ran a quantized model to save cost. Note: we sometimes call it the K-V cash in the transcript cause the auto-t does that.
2:48 - Dr. Kevin Li: Yeah we liked the batching and the cache, it really dropped token spend.
2:55 - Alex Chen: Can you share the headline performance + cost delta?
3:02 - Sofia Patel: On average latency dropped to sub-200ms for the 64-token median in our flows; cost per session decreased roughly 40% compared to our baseline host+lambda approach. Those are ballpark numbers — we have a spreadsheet, I'll share it.
3:25 - Jordan Brooks: That 40% figure is the one we pulled into the comms and it was a big win.
3:32 - Maya Alvarez: Important to say too that quality stayed the same, clinicians didn't see worse suggestions, if anything the model aligned better with our prompt sets.
3:45 - Alex Chen: Nice. Any funny hiccups or lessons we should highlight?
3:51 - Dr. Kevin Li: We initially misconfigured the VPC peering — and yes the dial-port settings were confusing, I kept saying V-P-Cee like a song. Redwood SEs helped troubleshoot and the logs were good enough to trace the issue.
4:12 - Sofia Patel: We had to tune the KV cache TTLs so we didn't leak session-specific info, privacy was top of mind.
4:20 - Maya Alvarez: We did an internal security review — SOC 2 matters a lot for us — and Redwood provided the compliance docs quickly which helped speed signoff.
4:33 - Alex Chen: On the security side, was there anything your audit team asked for beyond SOC 2?
4:38 - Maya Alvarez: A lot around audit logs, KMS integration, and data residency. We ended up using our own KMS and the private deployment controls felt solid.
4:51 - Jordan Brooks: For the marketing story we wanted a couple of quotes — like, 'reduced wait times by 30% and improved clinician satisfaction' — is that fair?
4:58 - Maya Alvarez: Yeah, fair. Maybe tweak to say 'reduced initial wait-times by ~30% and freed clinicians to focus on higher-value activity'.
5:10 - Alex Chen: Great quote. Quick note, we'll send suggested pull-quotes after this call for approvals.
5:18 - Jordan Brooks: Perfect.
5:24 - Alex Chen: Let's go into a bit more technical detail — Sofia, could you describe the model selection and fallback strategy?
5:30 - Sofia Patel: We used a tuned open model variant for the main path and a smaller quantized fallback when latency spiked. Redwood's smart routing allowed us to prefer cheaper variants during non-peak, and autoprobe fallbacks kept SLAs intact. There might be a note in the transcript where it says 'autoprobe' but we sometimes call it auto-prob or auto-probe.
5:56 - Dr. Kevin Li: The canary rollout helped us catch prompts that produced undesired suggestions. We set up an eval harness with sample prompts, which was super useful.
6:10 - Alex Chen: How did you measure clinician satisfaction?
6:14 - Maya Alvarez: We used weekly surveys plus a small manual audit of cases; our satisfaction metric went from 72% to 86% after the triage rolled out.
6:24 - Jordan Brooks: That stat is gold for the narrative.
6:27 - Alex Chen: Awesome. Switching to ops — Kevin, how was the deployment experience?
6:33 - Dr. Kevin Li: Pretty smooth overall. The Redwood Console dashboards gave us per-route latency breakdowns, token-level costs, and traces. We did see some confusing nomenclature in the early days — the auto transcription will probably say K V cash instead of KV cache — but the data was there.
6:55 - Sofia Patel: We also leveraged dedicated autoscaling policies to maintain throughput in morning peaks; that saved us from overprovisioning.
7:06 - Alex Chen: Did you ever need private/on-prem?
7:09 - Maya Alvarez: Not on-prem, but we deployed Private (VPC) with customer-managed networking. That satisfied legal and compliance.
7:18 - Jordan Brooks: For the case study visuals we want a screenshot of the console and one of the clinician flow — is that okay?
7:24 - Dr. Kevin Li: Sure, we can provide a sanitized screenshot.
7:28 - Alex Chen: Great — action item to share assets.
7:34 - Sofia Patel: I'll include low-res B-roll and the benchmark spreadsheet link.
7:40 - Alex Chen: Marketing outcomes — Jordan, you mentioned adoption?
7:43 - Jordan Brooks: After launch we saw a 22% increase in completed intake flows, 30% fewer abandoned sessions, and the clinician team reclaimed roughly 6 hours per week collectively. Those are the numbers we want in the one-pager.
8:00 - Maya Alvarez: Just to add, net promoter improved a bit as well, though it's early.
8:06 - Alex Chen: Any concerns about publishing the story? Privacy? Legal signoff?
8:10 - Jordan Brooks: Legal is mostly OK, they'll want final quotes and a list of approved speakers.
8:15 - Maya Alvarez: We need to make sure patient data is never in the screenshots, obviously.
8:19 - Alex Chen: Totally. We'll redact and sanitize.
8:22 - Sofia Patel: Also, if you want, Redwood can provide an anonymized benchmark CSV for the blog post.
8:28 - Maya Alvarez: That could be useful.
8:31 - Alex Chen: Let's ask a few lighter questions for the podcast — Maya, what's been the team's favorite unexpected win?
8:36 - Maya Alvarez: Clinicians telling us they get better-rested notes — the AI prep of context made consults shorter and more focused, so that's been surprisingly popular.
8:46 - Jordan Brooks: From PR, we want an anecdote — any specific moment where the tech saved a case?
8:51 - Maya Alvarez: There was one night shift where the triage highlighted a high-risk pattern and escalated appropriately, clinician flagged it and intervened earlier than usual. Good PR material but we need to keep it anonymized.
9:07 - Alex Chen: Love that. Switching gears, any mention of competitors in the story?
9:11 - Dr. Kevin Li: We evaluated some clouds and a couple of APIs like OpenAI and Anthropic but chose Redwood for the production controls and cost profile.
9:22 - Alex Chen: Good to note.
9:25 - Jordan Brooks: Quick editing preference — we want a 10-12 minute edited piece for our site and a longer cut for internal sharing.
9:32 - Alex Chen: Noted. We'll produce a short and long edit.
9:36 - Sofia Patel: I'll follow up with the benchmark link and notes on quantization profiles we used.
9:42 - Alex Chen: Any final questions from Sunnyside?
9:45 - Maya Alvarez: No, just timeline for the asset deliverables.
9:49 - Alex Chen: We'll send audio + full transcript by Monday (2025-11-10). Then you'll have two business days to review quotes; Jordan will coordinate.
